value: Use the customer-specific price if one exists; otherwise the bulk price for the highest min_cases threshold met; otherwise the standard case price.
The tier discount applies when the line meets the tier's min_cases, the customer is active and credit_status is not 'hold'. It applies to standard and bulk prices, not to customer-specific prices.

An active scheme gives free cases (buy_cases -> free_cases, repeated) when the business date is within its validity, the customer's tier is eligible and credit_status is not 'hold'. Free cases are added to the quote line at zero price.
Quotes are in whole cases. Convert other units (pieces, dozens, kg, litres, bags, tins) to cases with the product's units and round up to the next whole case, noting the rounding on the line.

If only one active SKU fits the request, use it. Otherwise, if the brand or size is not stated and the customer has bought that product type before, use the SKU from their most recent order of that type. Otherwise ask the operator to clarify; never guess.
If a name matches more than one customer, ask which one; never guess.
Customers on credit hold may receive draft quotes, but with no discount or scheme, and the quote must carry a credit-hold warning.
For credit customers (not cash terms), warn when outstanding plus the quote total including GST exceeds the credit limit.
Do not create quotes for inactive customers; tell the operator instead.
Quote the full requested quantity; record available and shortage cases per line, with the next restock date and a substitute if one exists. Never reserve or allocate stock from a quote.
Unopened cases may be returned within 7 days of delivery with the invoice.
Orders are confirmed only by a human operator in the ERP. The assistant may only create draft quotes.
